chapter: Teaching, the 1951 Big Show and New York nights
title: Louie Bellson and Jimmy Jones on the Big Show
summary: Jimmy Jones accompanied Sarah Vaughan and haunted Duke and Strayhorn; only Nat could follow Louie Bellson's 'Skin Deep' closer on about eighty one-nighters.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: incidentally, Sarah was with this show, and Jimmie Jones was her accompaniest, and he just haunted Duke and Stray Horn. Little did I realize the direction he was taking, you know, because he just adored them, you know, he admired them so. But this was a great band.

Louie Bellson was so exciting, they couldn't get anybody but Nat to follow him. Listen, he was so exciting really, and on the show I don't have to tell you it was Peg Leg Bates, Timmie Rodgers, Patteson and Jackson, just all heavy weights in show business. But nobody could follow Louie Bellson but Nat.
They used to not even pay any attention to drum soloists (inaudible) until Louie got there. Then everybody in the band would turn around and watch, they couldn't believe what they were hearing.

That's right. They did 'Skin Deep,' he was doing 'Skin Deep' to close the show, and it was a blockbuster, you know. So nobody wanted to follow him, but Nat Cole. Nat would come in and take charge, because -- well, you know, he was a super, superstar. But that was a highlight of 1951 for me was working with this band. We did about 80 one nighters.
